To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best solutions for discovering cause effect relations in texts are the solutions that use a combination of patterns, ontologies and machine learning.

1) cause effect relations in natural language are expressed using many different patterns; 2) some patterns are more frequent than others; 3) there are many lexical expressions for causal dependencies, but only a few are studied; 4) the same expressions and patterns are used for non causal relations; 5) solutions combining patterns, ontologies and machine learning are more successful than those using only one of these approaches.

(i) there are many ways of expressing cause effect relations in a natural language text, (ii) there are several patterns and models that can be used for extracting cause effect relations, but they are not always accurate, (iii) there are several ways of combining the models and improving the accuracy, and (iv) some models are better than others in some domains, while some are not applicable to some other domains
